title: Sort with a rule passed in
description:
Write `void sortWith(std::vector<int>& values, bool (*comesBefore)(int, int))`.

It sorts the vector so that for any two neighbours `a` then `b`, `comesBefore(b, a)` is false. In other words the caller decides the order by passing a function that answers "should the first argument come before the second?"

Write the sort yourself (selection sort is fine: find the element that should come first, swap it to the front, repeat for the rest). Do not use `std::sort`.
lessonTitle: Function Pointers, Callbacks and Command-Line Arguments
